g.text: Rail beyond: 3/4" ply x 18", 2x4 cap with foam pad

svg.text: D1 STOP BAR AND GRAVITY LATCH (SECTION)
1 1/2 in = 1 ft. Drawn square to the deck (deck shown level). Lane to the right.
6'-10 1/4" between rails
D2 STOP BAR FROM BEHIND (LOOKING DOWNHILL)
5/8 in = 1 ft. Both latch arms tie to one bridle on line B; line R ties to a ring at the bar center.
KEYED NOTES (D1, D2)
Stop bar: 2x4 on edge, 6'-9 5/8", painted
red so it is easy to check.
3" butt hinges (2), lane-side bottom edge,
1'-0" from each end: folds toward the lane.
Over-travel block, 1 1/2" sq: stops the bar
going past upright when it is reset.
Gravity gate latch on each rail's inner face,
about 1'-6" clear of the ball at this height.
Hooked tip drops in front of the bar top; its
sloped back lets the bar push past on reset.
On release the ball knocks the bar flat
and rolls over 1 1/2" of bar.
Rail beyond: 3/4" ply x 18", 2x4 cap
with a foam pad.
Bridle ring: both latch arms to line B
and the T-handle.
Ring at the bar center for line R (reset).
1/4" screw eyes (2), 1 1/2" apart
Kabuki pin: 1/4" smooth steel rod,
4" long, eye at the pull end
1" webbing loop sewn to the drape top,
hangs on the pin between the eyes
LINE K: pulling 3" frees every pin
D3 KABUKI PIN STATION (FRONT)
3 in = 1 ft. One of 6 stations along the batten.
10'-10" batten and drape
L1
L2
Pulley; line K leads back into the booth
D4 BATTEN, PINS, AND LINES (FRONT)
9/16 in = 1 ft. Line K runs along all 6 pins and out over the right outrigger; L1 and L2 fly the batten.
HOW THE TRIGGER WORKS
1. Armed: the bar stands upright between the rails, held by two gravity latches. The ball rests against it and pushes with only
about 2 1/2 lb (12 lb ball on a 12 deg slope), so the latches and the pull see very little load.
2. The drape hangs on 6 webbing loops, one over each kabuki pin. Every pin points the same way along the batten and is tied to line K.
3. The operator pulls one T-handle (A-6). Line K moves 3" and all 6 pins slide out of their loops together: the drape falls.
Line B has 2" of extra slack, so it lifts the latch arms a moment later: the bar is free, the ball knocks it flat and rolls.
4. The drape is heaped on the lane floor in about 1 s; the ball reaches the drape line at about 2.6 s.
5. Reset: haul the ball up past the bar (line H), pull line R to stand the bar up (the latches click over it), ease the ball down
onto the bar, trip the snap shackle, re-hang the drape on the lowered batten, fly it out, and set line K's slack. See A-8.
GYM HAUNTED HOUSE: HIDDEN BALL DROP (GROUP 4)
Mechanism details: stop bar and kabuki drop
Scale: as noted (on a 17 x 11 in sheet)
Planning sketch: verify every dimension on site before cutting.
